rules: Only visible player actions affect trust; never infer romance from high trust.
Jace cannot bypass the explicit consent and apology requirements.
Medical treatment cannot depend on relationship scores.
Romance opens in chapter 12 only on clear, affirmative, named intent; ambiguity triggers a clarifying in-character response, not a random match.
Any path can reach verified core facts and a complete ending.

beats.story_and_character_beat: Jace realizes his media stunt invaded your space; apologizes without expecting forgiveness. Alexander tries to shield the team but learns not to control your work.
Alexander presents his signed NDA and makes room for an honest interview. He admits responsibility, not an excuse.
Jace accepts team discipline and refuses a defensive PR script; trust grows only if his actions change.
Ethan asks for care without using his vulnerability to seek romance. A medical hold is treated as the responsible choice.
Damon provides evidence with a verifiable chain of custody, refuses to request confidential tactics, and protects a witness.
Ryan recognizes the past statement was inaccurate and volunteers to correct the record. His guilt does not become the player’s obligation.
Alexander calls off play even at competitive cost; Ethan sees that safety matters more than appearing invulnerable.
Jace offers a personally damaging clip rather than let false accusations stand. Damon refuses to exploit it on the ice.
The trade changes both Jace and Damon’s daily routines. Rivalry becomes uneasy teamwork; neither has automatic access to your time.
The five men have different reasons to request a private conversation; the player can refuse without relationship penalties.
The team honors the safety protocol even with a title on the line. No player is made to choose between treatment and the player’s love.
Each man explicitly asks rather than assumes; player may choose romance, friendship, professional distance, or an undecided path.
